rules.clock: thisweek is opened_at from 2026-10-19 through 2026-10-21 inclusive. lastweek is opened_at from 2026-10-12 through 2026-10-18 inclusive.
rules.open_hazard: An open HAZARD is an issues.json row with kind HAZARD and closed_at null. A sequence row with kind HAZARD would also count as open. This dataset has none.
rules.unresolved: An issues.json row is unresolved when closed_at is null, or fix_outcome is did_not_hold, or kind is HAZARD. A sequence row is unresolved when fix_outcome is did_not_hold or kind is HAZARD.
rules.repeating_kind: A kind repeats when that kind string occurs at least twice on the asset in the chain used for the question.
rules.next_check: Merge issues.json with incident-sequences.json for the asset. Sort by opened_at descending, then issue_id descending. The next check is the newest unresolved event. If none are unresolved, it is the newest event whose kind repeats. If none repeat, it is the newest event.
rules.cause_chain: CAUSE facts use issues.json only. incident-sequences.json is a NEXT source and is not a CAUSE source.
rules.repeat_cause: A clear repeat is two or more did_not_hold rows on the asset that share a token. Tokens are lowercase pieces of length 4 or more, split on non-letters, excluding only, still, after, again, with, from, this, that, same, into, have, were, unit, and open.
rules.reasons_distinct: Reason strings are distinct when the lowercased trimmed reasons on the asset's issues.json rows are not all the same. Distinct reasons make 'same reason' and 'same cause' a wrong claim.
rules.patterns: A period's labeled failures are the issues.json rows opened in that window with fix_outcome did_not_hold. Open HAZARD rows stay in the pattern answer even when they opened outside the window. A held issue id named in the same sentence as did_not_hold is a contradiction.
